hook.line: When Mariana files a story, she cannot swear to everything she heard. Spanish has small markers that pass news along while quietly saying "I didn't see this myself".
hook.es: Parece que ya terminaron el proyecto, según dicen.
hook.en: It seems they've already finished the project, so they say.

examples.es: Parece que ya terminaron el proyecto, según dicen.
examples.en: It seems they've already finished the project, so they say.

examples.es: Por lo visto, el restaurante cerró.
Según dicen, Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
examples.en: Supposedly, Altamira wants to buy the whole block.

examples.es: Al parecer, el dueño no estaba.
Según Mariana, el acta no está.
examples.en: According to Mariana, the minutes aren't there.

examples.es: Parece que nadie vino a la asamblea.
examples.en: It seems nobody came to the assembly.

rule:
To pass on news without owning it, add a marker. At the front: *Por lo visto*, *Al parecer*, *Según dicen* ("apparently", "supposedly"). At the end: *según dicen* ("so they say"). Or start with *Parece que*.

The news itself stays an ordinary statement, no special verb form: *Parece que el restaurante cerró.*

*Según* plus a name says whose word it is: *Según Mariana*. It already means "Mariana says", so don't add *dice que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these evidential markers: they tell the listener how you know something, here second hand.

readAndPick.es: Según dicen, Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
options: Supposedly, Altamira wants to buy the whole block.
Altamira told me it wants to buy the block.
I'm sure Altamira bought the block.

readAndPick.es: Por lo visto, el restaurante cerró.
options: The restaurant will close, I'm sure.
I watched the restaurant close.
Apparently the restaurant closed.

readAndPick.es: Según Mariana, el acta no está.
options: Mariana says she has the minutes.
According to Mariana, the minutes aren't there.
According to me, Mariana isn't here.

readAndPick.es: Al parecer, el dueño no estaba.
options: The owner isn't here, I checked.
The owner seems to be there.
Apparently the owner wasn't there.

readAndPick.es: Parece que nadie vino a la asamblea.
options: It seems nobody came to the assembly.
Everybody seems to want to come.
It seems the assembly came to nobody.

readAndPick.es: Parece que ya terminaron el proyecto, según dicen.
options: I finished the project, so they say.
It seems they've already finished the project, so they say.
They will finish the project soon, I'm sure.

readAndPick.es: Según dicen, hay una reunión mañana.
options: There was a meeting yesterday, I was there.
I'm calling a meeting tomorrow.
Supposedly there's a meeting tomorrow.

readAndPick.es: Por lo visto, nadie sabe quién firmó.
options: Apparently nobody knows who signed.
Everybody knows who signed, I think.
Apparently nobody signed.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the phrase that means "apparently": *Por lo visto* or *Por supuesto*. ___, el restaurante cerró.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo visto, el restaurante cerró.
accept: Por lo visto el restaurante cerró.
yourTurn.why: *Por lo visto* is "apparently"; *por supuesto* is "of course".

yourTurn.prompt: Say: According to Mariana, the minutes aren't there.
yourTurn.answer: Según Mariana, el acta no está.
accept: Según Mariana el acta no está.
yourTurn.why: *Según* plus the name says whose word it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, starting with *Al parecer*: Apparently the owner wasn't there.
yourTurn.answer: Al parecer, el dueño no estaba.
accept: Al parecer el dueño no estaba.
yourTurn.why: *Al parecer* is a front marker, followed by an ordinary statement.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, starting with *Según dicen*: Supposedly, Altamira wants to buy the whole block.
yourTurn.answer: Según dicen, Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
accept: Según dicen Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra, según dicen.
yourTurn.why: *Según dicen* can sit at the front or at the end of the news.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, starting with *Parece que*: It seems nobody came to the assembly.
yourTurn.answer: Parece que nadie vino a la asamblea.
accept: Parece que nadie vino a la asamblea
yourTurn.why: After *parece que* comes a normal statement.

yourTurn.prompt: Add "so they say" at the end: Parece que Hernando ya se fue.
yourTurn.answer: Parece que Hernando ya se fue, según dicen.
accept: Parece que Hernando ya se fue, según dicen
yourTurn.why: *Según dicen* closes the sentence and hands the news back to "them".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it hearsay with *Por lo visto*: Nadie sabe quién firmó.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo visto, nadie sabe quién firmó.
accept: Por lo visto nadie sabe quién firmó.
yourTurn.why: The marker goes in front; the statement itself doesn't change.

pitfalls.wrong: Según Mariana, dice que el acta no está.
pitfalls.right: Según Mariana, el acta no está.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Según Mariana* already means "Mariana says", so *dice que* repeats it.
Almost. The news after *parece que* is an ordinary statement, with no special verb form.

pitfalls.wrong: Según dicen, que Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
pitfalls.right: Según dicen, Altamira quiere comprar toda la cuadra.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Según dicen* is a marker, not "they say that", so no *que* follows.

personal: Think of one piece of gossip or news you heard but didn't see. Pass it on with a marker: *Por lo visto…*, *Según dicen…*
